pre-push jobs: load-aware parallelism

Issue #4085. The unit stage of bin/git-hooks/pre-push used to run 8 test files at once no matter what the machine was doing. Drag the inputs to see what resolve_pre_push_jobs picks now, and what the stage banner prints so a log names it.

Inputs

Presets:

Result

8

How it got there

    Stage banner

    
    
    
  
    

  
    
    
    The formula
    
    
    ORK_PRE_PUSH_JOBS set to a positive integer  ->  that
otherwise                                    ->  max(1, min(ncpu, 8, ncpu - round(load1)))
load unreadable                              ->  max(1, min(ncpu, 8))
    
    
    
      Rounding is half-up (5.4 rounds to 5, 5.5 to 6), done in awk because bash integer arithmetic
      cannot parse a fractional load. A non-numeric or zero override is ignored with a WARN, never honoured:
      xargs -P 0 means unbounded.
    
    
  
    

  
    
    
    What the fix answers (measured 2026-09-13, 5-minute load 37)
    
    
    
      
    fileinside pre-push (8 jobs)standalonereal cause
    
      
        
    tests/unit/test-image-paste-guard.sh1 of 68 failed, 213 s22/22 in 11 s5 s per-hook budget hit under load; now honours ORK_HOOK_TIMEOUT
    
        
    security: sqlite-injection10/1616/16run-hook.mjs 100 ms stdin watchdog ran the hook on {}, no row stored; now logged as "hook timed out after 0.1s"
    
        
    security: permission-mode-matrix16/1717/17same watchdog; helper returned its abstain as a verdict; now answers ERROR with the cause
    
          
    
    
    
    
      No assertion was weakened and no default was raised. The job count backs off so the runner stops being the thing
      that makes the gates flake, and the helpers name a timeout as a timeout instead of as a wrong verdict.
